title: Token-to-Chart Change Management RFC and Review Checklist
creator: Asha Patel
description: RFC to define a repeatable, low-risk workflow for making breaking changes to design tokens that affect charts and data visualizations (colors, spacing, typography, numeric scales). Covers contribution guidelines, automated validation, deprecation windows, and migration tooling to avoid visual regressions in customer-facing dashboards.
background: Design tokens are the single source of truth for brand, color, spacing and typography. Recently, several token changes intended to improve contrast and reduce flicker had unexpected surface-level regressions in charts and tables. Charts are particularly sensitive because tokens map to numeric scales, thresholds and small shapes. We need a formalized process that prevents surprise regressions while enabling the design system to evolve.
scope: This RFC covers token changes that impact charts, tables, and micro-visualizations: color palettes, semantic color aliases used in legends and thresholds, baseline spacing used by axes and gridlines, and typographic scales used in labels. It defines contributor guidance, review checklist, automated tests, deprecation policy, and migration support (codemods and pinned aliases).
out_of_scope: Component API contract changes (props surface), runtime chart library upgrades (handled by ENG tickets), and non-visual token changes such as build-only tokens.
acceptance_criteria: A clear CONTRIBUTING step-by-step for token changes affecting charts exists in the design repo
Automated visual regression tests added to the CI pipeline for flagged chart flows
A deprecation policy with a minimum 4-week migration window for any removed/renamed token
Codemod(s) or migration guidelines published for the top 3 consumer repos
At least one pilot token change executed end-to-end with no production regressions
review_checklist: Design: rationale doc + use-cases demonstrating why token change is necessary
Design: token map showing old -> new semantic aliases and recommended fallbacks
Engineering: unit tests for token resolution paths and snapshot coverage for chart components
QA: automated visual diff baseline and target viewports including high-DPI and 800x600
Accessibility: contrast ratio report for all semantic colors used in charts and thresholds
Performance: ensure token substitution does not add runtime recompute >5% on hot paths
Migration: codemod available or documented manual migration steps
Rollout: canary plan for dashboards and feature flags for shipping changes behind control toggle
Docs: changelog entry, upgrade notes, and examples showing before/after visuals
rollout_plan: Stage 1 — RFC signoff and test harness: land token aliases and add visual test baselines to CI
Stage 2 — Canary: enable new token mapping behind flag for 10% of internal dashboards and monitor regressions
Stage 3 — Migration tools: release codemod and migration guide to consumer teams; open office hours
Stage 4 — Gradual enforcement: after migration window, begin replacing old tokens in core components and mark old tokens deprecated
Stage 5 — Retirement: remove deprecated token aliases after 90 days and ship final changelog
migration_steps: Create alias tokens: keep old names but point them to new semantics to avoid immediate breakage
Publish design-token release with both alias and new canonical tokens and semantic mapping
Run codemod in consumer repos for replacing deprecated aliases (automated PRs where possible)
QA owners validate visual diffs and accessibility reports on PRs
Coordinate with platform/infra to ensure canary flagging is configured on Redwood Console dashboards
evaluation_metrics: Number of consumer PRs generated by codemod vs manual patches
% of dashboards passing visual regression suite before and after change
Incidents or customer bugs flagged that trace to token change
Time-to-migrate (median days) for top 10 consumer repos
decisions: Adopt a minimum 4-week migration window for any token rename/removal affecting charts
Prefer additive aliases over immediate replacement to maintain stability
Require automated visual regression tests for any token change that touches chart components
Mandate contrast checks for any semantic color change used in thresholds or labels
